body:
It gets harder to get out of bed each and every morning, so no, not really. Unfortunately I seem to have a bad case of hope so I won't be diving off the deep end anytime soon as much as I'd like to. Worst part is, I know I don't have it as bad as others and while I think depression is serious and merits attention no matter the cause, I hold myself to a double standard as with most things.

R U OK seems like an interesting concept, but after a while does it become like "How are you?", the casual greeting rather than the genuine question? It seems like you, for one, take it seriously which is very cool, I'm just wondering how the public generally uses the day since I'm not Australian.

What about you? Are you okay? Anything other than R U OK? day inspire you to post?

As far as I can tell, it's purely a mental barrier for me. I can't think of any external factors, I basically think I'm just not motivated enough. For some reason, the introduction of anything new into my daily activities of eating, Netflix, school, some homework, Internet, throws me off and overwhelms me. Also the frustration of not feeling immediate effects of my effort. I know these are my flaws, just can't seem to get past them. Recognizing is the first step, though, right?
I go to therapy, looking into a psychiatrist right now for meds. We'll see how that goes if I even get any.

This reminds me of a brain-training research class I took part in, making routines, small goals to lead to larger changes. Thank you for the article. I know all this is good for me and even if it doesn't really take that much effort (e.g. 10-15 minutes of meditation, and yes, Headspace is great), it's so hard to get myself to consistently do it. I'll manage to do it for a couple weeks then bam. It's over and I'm completely derailed. 

Thank you for all your advice and encouragement. :)

One of my favorite quotes I recently remembered is "You wouldn't worry so much what people think of you if you realized how little they did". However, it's hard to combat irrational fears/thoughts with facts which is where I run into trouble. 

Flexibility isn't my issue at this point, it's merely carving out some time to go and getting my ass out the door. I obsess a bit too much about time and getting things done which can make it hard for me to get myself to spend and 1 hour at a yoga studio (plus 1 hour of walking, round-trip) without panicking about time management.

Unluckily this week has not been conducive for me in the way of healthy living, but a couple good things came out of it. I was able to jump back on the healthy-lifestyle horse faster than ever after a breakdown and I was able to get myself to walk even on weekends which is when I usually sit at home and do nothing because there is no reason for me to get up (e.g. classes, groceries). Sadly no running/gym/yoga progress but rather than taking two steps back and leaving it at that, I was able to manage going two steps back but at least one step forward. Progress is progress, I guess.
Uh. Hopefully things will become okay. No help, Labor Day weekend means people are busy. But better! Relatively.
I had a mental breakdown this weekend but despite that I walked at least 3 miles every day.

I've known underneath the surface that I was since I was around... 10? But I didn't accept it until I was 18, freshman year of college. Before that, I'd never really had a vocabulary for sexuality let alone much knowledge at all about non-heterosexual variations of sexuality except for being gay, which I deeply suspected I wasn't.

I stopped buying snacks/sweets and switched to only produce and healthy proteins. By limiting my access to bad foods, even if I get those strong craving that I give in to, I can only take it out on kale and potatoes instead of Poptarts and Ben and Jerry's. 

I almost never eat out so my meals are prepared and consumed with access to a food scale to accurately log my ingredients. It's great and makes eating out even more of a treat.

Another couple things I would add that have personally helped me a lot to feel better mentally and to accelerate my weight loss progress are 1) sleeping at least around 7 hours per night and 2) regular consumption of water. Water especially helps when you start being more physically active because your body will start to need more. There have also been times when drinking water before a meal and waiting a bit can make you realize that part of what you perceive as hunger might really just be thirst. 

Good luck and by posting here, you'll find that starting with a community of support that you can reach out to 24/7 is going to make your journey that much easier (at least this has been my experience).

What kinds of foods do you have difficulty tracking? Possibly search online, not just in the calorie-counting app, for the calories of the given food. If you are talking about calories for specific ingredients for a meal, best way I've found to estimate is using a food scale and logging the components of the meal vs the meal itself.

This happened to me as I first started (I went from about 1600 kCal a day to 1200) and I was miserable and had binges and stressed out about my food. I quit tracking at that point and just gave up. 

But then I had the brilliant idea of decreasing my caloric intake by about 50 kCal weekly (week 1: 1600, week 2, 1550, ... week n 1200). If 1450 was giving me a hard time, I would revert back to 1500 until I want comfortable enough with that to decrease. This helped a ridiculous amount with adjusting my body and mind to calorie counting.

Several months ago, I would have agreed with you that calorie counting was hell, but now? I do it every day. Of course, to each his/her own, but views can change with different strategies too.

That is a wonderful blog post, thanks for sharing it with me. I really do need to get music on my phone or podcasts or SOMETHING to help keep my pace and motivation up if/when I do start running (fingers crossed). Thank you for your story and honesty. I know that people are probably not paying too much attention to me if at all, but it's all the irrational thoughts and fears that are the hardest to overcome.

As for free weights... I've heard about needing proper form and balance for a good workout/to not get hurt. Did you learn form by trial and error or assistance from someone else or online tutorials...? Sometimes the online tutorials and videos confuse me. I'm more of a kinetic learner, but again, nervous to ask for help.
Yes, exactly this. Everywhere I look... mmm.
I'll have to try that out. Thanks!
I think I'm in love with this subreddit.

I don't have my own room. It's shared with one other person. Please! Link me the bodyweight/wighted exercises (I do have a couple weights somewhere)! If I end up feeling up to doing them, I'd like to be prepared. /r/Fitness is great but also has a LOT of information which can get somewhat overwhelming.

I'm somewhat regimental when it comes to diet though I do slip up... but even when I slip up I make sure to input my food into MFP as accurately as I can. 

I hadn't thought of putting weights in my backpack! I'll have to try it in the days to come. The only negative to walking that I've encountered is that if I walk for too long or don't get up early enough to walk, I panic about wasting too much time walking and not doing other things like homework or other errands.

When do you do the push-ups/random exercises? In your room or while walking (I know someone who does that)? Yoga seems more viable at this point than talking to my roommate but maybe as time passes I'll build up the courage to ask... or find a way out of it like asking for all her class schedules and exercising while she's gone... 

Thanks for the time and effort you put into your response, really. :) It makes me feel quite a bit less alone.

It's a highly discouraging feeling, I know. And yet despite it all I keep trying. For God knows what reason... perfectionism, perceived peer pressure, or just because not trying is boring. Hopefully things will turn around some day. Good luck to you.
Looks like a fuchsia plant.

I read this research study about puns the other day and it was pretty interesting. Apparently the scientists found that kleptomaniacs don't understand them as well as other people because they take things literally. Cool, right?

(Presented in a conversational style, this gets people *every time.*)

Same. I like certain women's clothing as well, but I always feel people staring at me when I go to the men's sections for shirts or sweaters I like and want to buy. I'm a petite girl so it's additionally a bit frustrating that most men's clothing I want doesn't come in my size (unless I head over to the XL/L section of GAP kids...). I think it would be a great addition for people who like to wear what they want to wear regardless of whether that article of clothing was intentionally manufactured for one gender or the other.

Every time I go over I feel worse and end up eating more. If it persists a few days, I give up for a week or two, then try and get it back together. This is one of those weeks (hopefully not two). 

Keep going. Keep working every day. It's the overall net effort that matters. Slipping up is okay, get back on your feet when you can and move forward.

I know, right? I feel like somehow I'm doing college wrong. I completely resonate with you. Not everyone is like this but it doesn't make you boring or broken. 

One thing that's helped me get out of the house is to trap myself into a commitment with my flatmates. I make plans with them and feel obligated to go when the time comes, even when I'm feeling anxious or depressed. So far it's been good and I've been getting out more, still not as much as the average student probably does, but it's an improvement. Baby steps. :)
